novelty_flags.label: thm:hall-characterization
novelty_flags.one_line: The antidiagonal support is a staircase pattern after reindexing, so Dahl2008's published fixed-margin staircase feasibility characterization already covers the mathematical Hall kernel; retain it as an attributed supporting specialization, not an independent novelty claim.

soundness_flags.label: ass:censoring-exchangeability
soundness_flags.one_line: C ⟂ U conditional on R makes censoring independent of the entire cross-world response tree and is stronger than the cited standard arm-specific/sequential CAR condition; weaken it to the factual-arm censoring condition needed for identification and make the lift preserve that condition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:capped-capacity and all sharpness/value claims
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The joint-capacity restriction B+W≤H is an externally prespecified, scientifically justified sensitivity restriction rather than a consequence of separate capping.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All Hall, endpoint, causal-lift, joint-value, regret, and confidence claims are conditional on the externally prespecified capacity-sensitivity model; any SPRINT use remains conditional on a credible prespecified finite-reserve interpretation.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1840 abstract; p. 1841 support-condition theorem and Section 3 description
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article characterizes nonemptiness for transportation matrices with fixed row and column sums under a staircase support pattern and gives construction algorithms; the proposal's antidiagonal support is such a staircase after reversing one order.

source_verification_receipts.locator: main.tex, Proposition 1 lines 333–348 and Corollary 1 lines 354–361
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited source distinguishes full CAR from sequential CAR and identifies the standard factual-arm censoring condition as independence of the arm-a full path and its arm-a censoring variable conditional on A=a, restricted to the censoring-before-failure region; it does not call unconditional independence of one observed censoring time from an entire response tree the standard condition.

Assumption 1 equates the switched post-landmark recurrent-event increment distribution among intensive survivors with the sustained-standard increment distribution among standard survivors; Proposition 1 gives quantile-trimming bounds and the article defines regime value and regret.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Sections 1–3, especially lines 52–86 and 177–208
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies fixed-marginal sum/difference CDF bounds, distinguishes pointwise sharpness from attainment, and treats the discrete-margin case; it does not impose the proposal's antidiagonal support restriction.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies corrected proof, published 17 February 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies treatment choice under partial identification in a Gaussian-likelihood decision framework and characterizes minimax-regret rules, including least-randomizing optimal rules.

The published article develops regularized support-function inference for components of polygonal affine identified sets with uniform Gaussian behavior at flat faces; it is a general inference antecedent rather than the proposed recurrent-event transport construction.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the global response-tree censoring independence with the exact arm-specific sequential-CAR or independent-censoring condition required for the observed margins, then state and verify the modified lift against that weaker condition.
Recast the Hall criterion as an explicitly attributed Dahl specialization and foreground the causal lift plus the open-family shared-law versus scalar-regret separation as the paper's novel kernel.

Add a concrete externally elicited finite-reserve mechanism and cap-selection protocol for the intended clinical setting, including a sensitivity range whose Hall feasibility can be empirically checked before policy analysis.

recommended_next_step: Revise the censoring assumption and novelty framing of the Hall lemma, then advance the retained field-tier shared-law causal-regret kernel to Stage 0.
